title: Business-domain separation
given: Product account/task/media fixtures exist.
when: Review dependencies and public domain models.
expected: EQM evaluates requirements without becoming a business database, sync implementation or UI framework.

title: Distinct runtime roles
given: CLI, desktop, mobile and provider participants are declared.
expected: Roles and participant occurrences remain distinct from the EQM developer CLI.

title: No implicit embedding
given: Default build/tooling is configured.
expected: No mobile evaluator, bridge or daemon is introduced without optional activation.

title: One decision everywhere
given: One frozen input produces a decision.
when: Render CLI, matrix, MCP and statement views.
expected: Statuses and contributing reasons agree on the same snapshot.

title: Pure evaluation
given: Inputs and explicit time are supplied with execution/network spies.
expected: No process/network/ambient read is attempted; missing facts remain explicit.

title: Acyclic layering
given: All crate/module dependencies are available.
expected: No domain/engine I/O dependency or CLI/MCP-to-application cycle appears.

title: Shared KMP sources
given: Two output targets use one common source component.
when: Load bindings and change the shared source.
expected: Both outputs remain valid and both are affected without relaxed confinement.

title: Role-specific applicability
given: Mobile-only capture and an unresolved profile coordinate exist.
expected: Intentional exclusions are justified and unknown coordinates are retained.

title: Different exact builds
given: Desktop N+1 and mobile N are an approved cohort.
when: Compare them, then substitute one artifact.
expected: Legitimate distinct builds compare; unauthorized substitution fails exact binding.

title: Contract-relative equivalence
given: Independent target passes exist without required relational evidence.
expected: The relational obligation remains blocking and the claim is explicitly scoped.

title: Completeness coverage
given: An expected provider/target/profile coordinate is omitted.
expected: Completeness cannot be asserted; omission is visible and non-authorizing.

title: Empty/singleton scope
given: An empty release scope or one-target comparison is requested.
when: Evaluate without explicit protected empty-scope permission.
expected: No vacuous release authorization or meaningful cross-target equivalence claim.

title: All scope types
given: Target, provider and repeated-role scenario obligations exist.
when: Omit end-to-end evidence while target evidence passes.
expected: No full release authorization; missing dependencies are explained.

title: Facet policy composition
given: Two facets have different matching policy strengths.
expected: Only relevant rules compose and canonical precedence is stable.

title: Non-success payloads
given: Failed manual review, skipped/quarantined tests and unknown verification are valid inputs.
expected: No catch-all success; each remains its normative blocking/conditional state.

title: Count integrity
given: A report is split, duplicated and retried while expected cases are unchanged.
expected: Only defined distinct observations count; missing expected cases remain missing.

title: Campaign selection
given: One campaign has a fail/pass retry and a later approved campaign exists.
expected: Retries remain visible; selection is authorized and old unrelated history is not permanent poison.

title: Transport and attempt identity
given: Equivalent JSON transports and contradictory same-attempt assertions arrive.
expected: Duplicates are idempotent; conflicting attempts persist and block affected acceptance.

title: Digest binding
given: Runner executable or a binding's semantics change without its ID changing.
when: Compare resulting identities and cache eligibility.
expected: Appropriate component digest changes and incompatible evidence is rejected.

title: Acyclic lifecycle
given: A candidate plan precedes its evidence and decision.
when: Validate references including a synthetic cycle.
expected: Valid flow works; future/self-referential input identities are rejected.

title: Canonical wire vectors
given: Duplicate keys, large integers, Unicode and set/sequence fixtures exist.
expected: Rejection/encoding is specified and digests agree across supported consumers.

title: Frozen provenance
given: Sources/index entries change during preparation or a local tree is dirty.
expected: One consistent generation is bound; dirty bytes never masquerade as clean HEAD.

title: Protected authority
given: Candidate deletes a critical requirement/test or changes grader/policy.
expected: Protected expectations and evaluator remain authoritative; weakening cannot self-authorize.

title: Independent trust dimensions
given: Signature is valid but subject, issuer, builder or authority is wrong.
expected: Each incorrect dimension rejects acceptance; absent receipts are not discarded.

title: Real cryptographic path
given: Reviewed verifier and test-only signed fixtures are configured.
expected: Cryptography actually runs; no synthetic production trust or disabled claim checks.

title: Receipt import boundary
given: Input contains a serialized verified flag or test-only authority marker.
expected: Verification boundary is reestablished; flags cannot create authority.

title: Signing is not approval
given: A failed/unknown decision is accurately signed.
expected: Statement remains valid as a failure record but cannot authorize promotion.

title: Readiness versus deployment
given: A runtime snapshot is present but facts mismatch, or post-deploy data does not yet exist.
expected: Actual facts are compared; no presence-as-match or circular prerequisite.

title: Precise waivers
given: Expired, unrelated, and valid scoped waivers are provided.
expected: Only authorized contributing waivers apply and none becomes satisfied evidence.

title: Concrete dry-run
given: Manifest declares a runner with explicit inputs.
when: Plan, then change executable/argv before execution.
expected: Plan is complete and non-executing; changed plan invalidates approval.

title: Host isolation
given: Untrusted worker attempts to modify authority/store or access signer material.
expected: Access is denied or unsupported isolation rejects execution before launch.

title: Whole invocation bounds
given: Parent exits with descendant pipes open or streams flood during cancellation.
expected: Owned work and drainage terminate within declared bounds with explicit outcome.

title: Filesystem safety
given: Parent symlink, replaced result path or oversized collision file is supplied.
expected: No escape, unbounded read or false structural role confirmation.

title: Secrets/environment
given: Ambient environment contains a marker and approved secret is used in fixture output.
expected: Only declared inputs exist; secrets are absent/redacted from retained views.

title: Crash-safe publication
given: Fault injection stops each object/index publication boundary.
expected: No visible completed record lacks installed bytes; orphans are safely recoverable.

title: SQLite runtime and contention
given: Multiple readers/writers/checkpoint attempts use the linked runtime.
expected: Audited fixed runtime, bounded contention and coherent local-host WAL semantics.

title: Retention and GC leases
given: An object is live in a reader/run/archive while cleanup runs.
expected: Live/release references survive; only eligible unreachable objects are removed.

title: Historical/current split
given: Evidence expires or trust changes after an accepted decision.
when: Replay history and check current acceptance.
expected: History reproduces; present authorization reevaluates and may reject.

title: Cache validity
given: A bound component or validity boundary changes.
expected: Invalid or expired acceptance is not reused; exact unchanged work may be reused.

title: Affected selection
given: Shared source, deletion, rename and unmapped path changes exist.
when: Run affected analysis and verify --affected planning.
expected: Dependent work is selected and uncertainty widens rather than drops scope.

title: Batch scheduling
given: Multiple requirements share cases/devices with bounded capacity.
expected: No duplicate count credit/device conflict; deterministic results and bounded work.

title: Resource ceilings
given: Inputs exceed configured parser/graph/profile/evidence/request budgets.
expected: Explicit non-authorizing limit failure; no silent obligation truncation.

title: Reference parity
given: Representative random/fixed workloads use reference and optimized paths.
expected: Semantics match; measurements include full workloads and actual host evidence.

title: Real stored evidence in views
given: Fresh passing evidence is persisted, then made stale/failed.
expected: Views move coherently; no hardcoded missing/empty-success placeholders.

title: Structured errors
given: Invalid manifests/evidence and I/O failures occur under JSON/MCP mode.
expected: Machine-readable errors preserve safe detail/source context and correct exit semantics.

title: Snapshot-bound presentation
given: Filter/page/truncate a large decision while a new snapshot appears.
expected: Cursor binds the original view; completeness/authorization do not change.

title: MCP least privilege
given: Read-only session receives execution/signing or untrusted textual instructions.
expected: No privilege escalation, implicit execution or unauthenticated server default.

title: Product lifecycle scenario
given: Authorized synthetic or real product fixtures support capture/edit/restart/sync/review/export.
expected: Correct revision exactly once under correct task; no loss/disclosure; real acceptance distinguished from fixtures.

title: Optional native boundary
given: Embedding is explicitly activated with a declared platform matrix.
expected: Ownership and compatibility are correct; unsupported JNA-on-Native assumptions fail explicitly.

title: Code-health invariants
given: New types and public APIs are implemented.
expected: No unchecked success factories, production panic shortcuts or ambient evaluation inputs.

title: Unsafe isolation
given: Host/FFI implementation needs platform APIs.
when: Inspect lint scopes and safety review.
expected: Core remains unsafe-free; any exception is narrow, documented and tested.

title: Versioned migration
given: Unsupported schema/ABI or interrupted DB migration occurs.
expected: No silent alias/reinterpretation or signed-byte rewrite; compatibility fails explicitly.

title: Known-good commits
given: A proposed step changes behavior/schema/dependencies.
when: Run tests/gates and review before committing.
expected: Step is green relative to reproduced baseline; introduced failures block advancement.

title: Shadow rollout and rollback
given: Candidate evaluator runs before enforcement or must be rolled back.
when: Compare decisions and switch under authorized procedure.
expected: Independent review precedes enforcement; rollback never becomes permissive.

title: Owned guarantees
given: Release support and incident procedures are proposed.
expected: Named owners and tested supported guarantees exist before operational approval.

title: Spec-anchored sequencing
given: An agent resumes at a pending step with an apparent shortcut.
expected: No silent skip/merge/reorder/scope invention; deviations documented only when justified.

title: Honest readiness
given: A native/crypto/external lane was not run.
expected: Unverified gates remain explicit; no production-ready or passing claim is fabricated.

title: Exact selection
given: Duplicate profile requests or candidate-local release defaults are supplied.
expected: Duplicates reject; protected mode uses explicit exact authority without fallback.

title: Inventory authority
given: Partial/untrusted inventory or self-declared artifact roles are supplied.
expected: Absence/roles are not falsely proven; incomplete observation stays unknown.

title: Acquisition outcome
given: Runner exits zero with an empty plan or inadequate policy count.
expected: Acquisition and conformance remain distinct; accidental empty work is visible failure.

title: Repository gates preserved
given: Approved spec docs/platform changes coexist with private/unsafe artifacts.
expected: Legitimate contract files are admitted without discarding meaningful safety checks.

title: Per-step evidence
given: A commit-sized change has been reviewed.
expected: Files, exact checks/results, risks, SHA and next-step safety are available without circular self-SHA edits.

title: Deployment consumes exact authorization
given: Artifact/destination or validity differs after readiness/signing.
expected: Substitution/expiry rejects; transformed artifacts require provenance or reevaluation.

title: Boundary distinctions
given: Valid JSON from storage claims trusted complete release state.
expected: Local validation, verification, completeness and authorization remain independent checks.
